summary: Suffolk County Aermotor LS-40 tower of 1930 near Amagansett; observers reported fires in 1935-36; closed 1959, removed 1960; land now privately held.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40, 73 ft tower per NYSFFLA list and Starr list; the register gives 73 ft concrete footings with steel structure, wood steps and landing platforms
facts.status_note: Dismantled and removed in 1960; the register says the land is now privately held; no source describes what remains on the site

staffing.status: Observer W.S. Miller reported fires and visitors in 1935 and 1936; the tower was closed in 1959

access.note: Register says the land is now privately held; no public access is described in the sources read

facts.agency: New York State Conservation Department; funds for the tower came from the Town of East Hampton and private subscription

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NYSFFLA list and Starr list give the tower as 73 ft; the register gives 73 ft concrete footings. height_m 22.3 follows the two lists; the story says the register's 73 feet describe the footings.
NYSFFLA list says a local demolition contractor removed the tower in 1960; the register credits the state Conservation Commission. Both agree on 1960.

Forest Lookouts records a transfer of title to Suffolk County in 1959; the register says the land is now privately held. The sources do not date when the land passed from county to private hands, so the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Brief status 'gone' and coordinates confirmed by the register. The NYSFFLA list spells the name 'Stoney Hill'; the brief and register use 'Stony'. No source describes the site today beyond 'privately held', so access is recorded as private. Search turned up East Hampton land-protection documents for Stony Hill Road parcels and an East Hampton Star piece; they were not fetched or linked to this tower, and are not used. No corrections to the brief.
